description.narrative:
Projektet avser att hjälpa Bosnien och Hercegovina att definiera och implementera SDG-målen / 2030-Agendan till handling genom att samla relevanta partner kring SDG ”Roadmap” - en agenda med en tydlig vision för landet.
Projektet har för syfte att bygga kapacitet och förbereda privata och offentliga partners i Bosnien och Hercegovina för genomförandet av SDGs, med två följande effektmål: 1. SDGs ”Roadmap” för BiH utvecklas och att genomförandet påbörjades. 2. att privat sektor aktörer är sensibiliserad och engagerad i SDGs prioritering, planering och genomförande.

The project aims to capacitate and prepare private and public sector partners in Bosnia and Herzegovina for the SDGs implementation, thus directly supporting Bosnia and Herzegovina’s efforts to contribute to the largest global agenda that exists today – Agenda 2030.

The Overall Goal of the intervention is that Bosnia and Herzegovina translates Agenda 2030 into action for the benefit of all its citizens. The Project Outcome is as follows: Public and private sector partners prepared for implementation of the SDGs in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
The project aims to capacitate and prepare private and public sector partners in Bosnia and Herzegovina for the SDGs implementation, thus directly supporting Bosnia and Herzegovina´s efforts to contribute to the largest global agenda that exists today Agenda 2030. The project envisages two outputs as follows: 1. SDG Roadmap for Bosnia and Herzegovina developed, and implementation started. 2. Private sector actors sensitized and engaged in SDGs prioritization, planning and implementation.

The project during its implementation has carried our coordinate and comprehensive activities that contributed to the execution of impressive project results. The approach that was applied recognizing the complex administrative and political situation in the country aiming at local ownership deemed to be successful. The project was attentive to division of competencies within the country resulting in strong local ownership of results achieved.
One of the key milestones at the initial stages of the project was the finalization of the first BIH Voluntary Review (VNR). The review was successfully developed by the designated working group consisting of all relevant representatives and relevant institutions at all administrative levels. In 2019, the BiH Delegation, presided by the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of BiH, presented the first VNR at the UN HLPF on Sustainable Development in New York.
The purpose of VNR informed on the process undertaken in the country regarding Agenda 2030 and the SDGs, which to date had engaged thousands of people, and provided baseline information for all 17 SDGs for BIH.
The main achievement in terms of results was related to the finalization and adoption of the SDGs Framework in BIH by the BiH Council of Ministers (April 2021). The document is result of multi-stakeholders consultations, extensive technical work necessary to base lines. The process was highly inclusive engaging not only representatives from all governance levels, but also civil society, academia and private sector. BiH Council of Ministers also appointed the SDG Council that will be responsible to coordinate, monitor and report the implementation of SGDs Framework for BIH.
The SDGs Framework is BiH is regarded as an important document that will enable localization of SDGs in BIH an serving as a unique opportunity to introduce a holistic approach to long-term development of the country. Moreover, taking into account political realities in BIH, SDG Framework can also be viewed as a country-wide document that creates synergies between Agenda 2030 and the EU requirements regarding domestic development priorities.
During the roll - out stage of the project, in 2017 the project supported the development of Rapid Integration Assessment and RIA report. This activity helped in achieving two results that are worth noting: a) wide range of relevant representatives received required training to conduct this type of exercise. b) 69 respective strategies on all levels of governance in the country, including the international partners such as the EU, WB, UN were screened to to match the indicators with the 10 SDG indicators allowing for comprehensive approach to future development.
When it comes to private sector engagement, similarly the project realized numerous activities aimed to reach the required results. The results that are worth noting is that engagement of private sector in activities related to Agenda 2030 and SDGs continued to grow over the years. Companies readily participated in trainings, business accelerators and decarbonisation challenges. In 2021, 24 companies developed their Annual Sustainability Reports. The project organized a open competition for SDG Business Pioneers Award that turned into a flagship event of the project. The activity was originally designed to serve as an incentive to business leaders to receive required trainings and also be awarded for their efforts in translating the SDGs in their operation. The interest to take part in the competition grew over the years and the interest among the stakeholders is continuously on the rise.
In terms of unexpected results, the actual results of the project in relation to the political realities of the country were not anticipated. At the time when very few documents were approved by the state level institutions due to political turmoil the project seceded in receiving fully fledged approval of documents and initiatives that were subject to state level approval. It is difficult to assesses as to why the project measured results in this regard but it can be noted that very inclusive and consultative approach may have received wide support among all stakeholders involved.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
